Today you act after the fall — because there's never been a practical way to act before it.

How this falls figure is estimated: Australia’s Star Ratings publishes falls as the percentage of residents who experienced one or more falls — not a count. We apply that published rate to an estimated bed base for each home (by size band: Small 20–40, Medium 45–75, Large 80–130 beds) and sum across the group, giving a conservative range of 27–44 with a median of 34 (shown above). It counts residents who fell, not total fall events, so the real number is likely higher. The $1,000 per-fall management burden is a conservative internal operating assumption.

01

Predict AI + your data

The AI pulls each resident's record from your Telstra Health system and cross-checks it against continuous signal from the bed, radar and toilet sensors — scoring fall risk around the clock.

02

Detect real-time alert

When a resident crosses their set mobility threshold, the in-charge staff are alerted in real time — a warning before the fall, not a report after it.

03

Act bedside + HG layer

At the bedside, staff act according to the care plan in the moment. Above it, the HG clinical team owns the oversight — escalating trends, flagging focus residents, recommending actions and delivering board-ready evidence.

So your clinical team stops watching dashboards — and starts acting on what matters. That's the HG layer no platform sells you.

The coach principle

Giving a home the tech without clinical consultant support is like handing a sports team video analytics and performance stats but no coach. The data is there — but the team keeps playing the same way.

A coach interprets the numbers, changes behaviours and lifts outcomes. That's the role the HG clinical team plays — moving your floor from reacting to incidents to preventing them.
